prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Conroe, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1115; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision you were involved in at the parking lot in Conroe. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Please describe where you were when the accident happened.

A: I was pulling out of a parking space near the main entrance of the store. It was a busy afternoon and the lot was pretty crowded.

Q: Which direction were you traveling, and what did you see before the impact?

A: I was backing out slowly and I checked my mirrors. I didn't see anything coming, but then I heard a horn and felt the impact on the driver's side of my car.

Q: What happened to your vehicle?

A: The other car hit my rear quarter panel. The door was dented and the back bumper came loose.

Q: Were you injured?

A: Yes. I tried to brace myself on the steering wheel and my right wrist took most of the force. I went to the urgent care clinic the same day and they said it was fractured.

Q: Have you received any medical treatment since then?

A: I have a splint and I'm seeing an orthopedic specialist next week. They said I may need a cast for several weeks.

Q: Did anyone at the scene give a statement or take photos?

A: I took photos of both cars and the parking space markings. The other driver exchanged insurance information with me, and a store employee came out to look.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the collision?

A: I just want to make sure my repair costs and medical bills are covered. I'm still having trouble using my right hand for everyday tasks.

Q: Thank you. We'll follow up once we review the photos and medical records. This concludes the statement.

A: Okay, thank you.
